prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals in the Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 (max 500 words)

Economy, tax, and pensions
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament; no rises to income tax or VAT rates.
- “Triple Lock Plus”: uprate both State Pension and a new age-related tax-free personal allowance for pensioners by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%; maintain existing pensioner benefits.
- Raise at least £6bn a year from tackling tax avoidance/evasion by end of Parliament.

Families and childcare
- 30 hours’ free childcare from nine months to school (fully rolled out by Sept 2025).
- Move Child Benefit to a household assessment: taper from £120,000 to £160,000 combined income.

Business, innovation, and trade
- Maintain full expensing; consider extending to leasing when affordable; no corporation tax increase.
- 10-point SME plan: business rates support, VAT threshold smoothing, easier finance (Open Finance, mutual banks), prompt payment enforcement, reduced reporting burdens; retain EIS/SEIS/VCTs and not increase CGT.
- Public R&D to £22bn/year; major AI compute investment; advanced manufacturing support; financial services reforms; new/free trade deals (e.g., India, GCC); use post‑Brexit regulatory reforms.

Public sector and welfare
- Reduce civil service to pre‑pandemic size; halve spend on consultants; boost digital/AI skills; departmental productivity plans.
- Welfare reform: revise PIP assessments; tighten Work Capability Assessments; overhaul fit notes; tougher sanctions at 12 months; complete Universal Credit rollout; new Fraud Bill.

Education and youth
- Protect per‑pupil schools funding; statutory ban on mobiles in the school day; expand teacher recruitment/retention payments.
- Advanced British Standard (more subjects; English and maths to 18).
- 100,000 more apprenticeships, funded by restricting low‑outcome degrees.
- Mandatory National Service at 18: either one year full‑time military/cyber (competitive, paid) or civic service (25 days).

Health and social care
- NHS funding to rise above inflation annually; train 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; expand Pharmacy First, 250 GP surgery projects, 50 Community Diagnostic Centres.
- £3.4bn NHS tech programme (NHS App, data platform, AI diagnostics); reduce managers by 5,500.
- Dental Recovery Plan (2.5m extra appointments; service obligation for new dentists).
- Women’s health actions; Major Conditions Strategy; Tobacco and Vapes Bill; implement Cass Review; single‑sex accommodation rights.

Border security, defence, and foreign policy
- Legal annual migration cap on work/family visas with yearly parliamentary vote; higher visa thresholds; health checks/IHS changes; increased fees; student dependant limits.
- Illegal migration: monthly Rwanda flights; implement Illegal Migration Act; expand returns and anti‑smuggler action; pursue international asylum reform.
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; at least £10bn for munitions; 5% of defence budget to R&D (plus 2% for exploitation); sustained support for Ukraine; Veterans’ Bill and measures.

Energy, climate, and environment
- Annual North Sea oil and gas licensing; maintain windfall tax until 2028–29 (with investment allowances).
- New gas power stations; treble offshore wind; launch first CCUS clusters; approve two SMR fleets within 100 days; new nuclear at Wylfa; interconnectors; £1.1bn Green Industries Growth Accelerator; carbon border adjustment by 2027.
- Keep price cap; review standing charges; Pumpwatch; local electricity markets; £6bn for home efficiency plus universal voucher scheme; onshore wind with local consent; protect best farmland for solar; no fracking.
- Water plan: tougher penalties, unlimited fines, river recovery fund; reform water price review.
- New National Park; tree/peatland funding; deposit return scheme; tougher fly-tipping penalties; restrict new waste incinerators.

Housing and communities
- 1.6m homes: scrap nutrient neutrality rules with mitigation fees; fast‑track brownfield in 20 largest cities; densify inner London; protect Green Belt.
- Stamp Duty relief for first‑time buyers up to £425k made permanent; new Help to Buy (up to 20% equity loan, 5% deposit); CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants (two years).
- Leasehold reform (cap/phase down ground rents); Renters Reform Bill (end Section 21 with court changes).
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; Martyn’s Law; tougher sentencing for serious crimes; hotspot policing; anti‑fraud measures.
- Drivers: ban road pricing by local/national government; reverse London ULEZ expansion; referendums for new 20mph/LTN schemes; extend £2 bus fare cap for the Parliament; Rail Reform (Great British Railways).

Agriculture, fisheries, rural
- Increase UK‑wide farming budget by £1bn over the Parliament; legally binding food security target; 50% public food spend local/high‑standard; fast‑track farm infrastructure; extend Seafood Fund (£100m equivalent), with support for inshore fleets.

Union and devolution
- Continue direct UK investment across Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland (UKSPF extension, town endowments, Freeports/Investment Zones); protect UK internal market; implement Windsor Framework; improve UK‑wide data comparability.
